thread:
anya: quick idea — proposal to surface a per-customer 'cost_slate' policy that lets routing prefer cheaper model builds for low-tier traffic when predicted token-cost > threshold. minimal config, controlled by a slider in console.
kevin: hmm, how do we decide "cheaper"? lower-precision quantized models or smaller architecture?
anya: both, but prefer same-architecture quantized variants first. fallback order: full -> q4 -> q2_small -> distilled. decision made by estimated tokens * p95_model_cost. if > customer_budget_threshold then attempt degrade.
lia: console UX: can we add a preview that shows "expected monthly savings" + "expected quality delta"? PMs want concrete numbers before enabling. :eyes:
sahil: telemetry must expose a new metric: effective_token_cost and cost_savings_pct per route + per-customer. also show #requests downgraded and rollback rate. we'll need a histogram for latency delta after degrade.
ravin: rollout: feature flag on/off per org, start with 5 customers, canary for region eu-west first. need a kill switch that pins route to original model instantly.
anya: agreed. API sketch for routing policy (proposal):
```json
{"policy_name": "cost_slate_v1", "priority": 10, "rules": [{"match": "tier == 'free' || tier == 'starter'", "allow_degrade": true, "degrade_order": ["q4f", "q2s"], "cost_threshold_cents_per_token": 0.001}, {"match": "region == 'apac'", "region_penalty_multiplier": 1.2}], "telemetry_labels": ["route","model_variant","org_id"]}
```
kevin: tiny nit: using absolute cents/token thresholds is ok but we'll also want relative budget share (eg 5% of monthly commit) since commits vary widely.
lia: for console controls: slider 0-100% for "willingness to degrade" + a checkbox "apply region penalties" + a link to an "impact preview" modal. also expose per-route quick revert button.
sahil: telemetry plumbing: emit events on attempt_to_degrade, degrade_success, degrade_quality_regression (if eval set triggers), and revert_by_operator. export to metrics store with tags. we should also add a sample rate for full request traces to avoid SLO blowups.
ravin: rollout plan steps: create policy, enable feature-flag gate, canary 5 orgs, daily quality-dashboard check, expand to 25%, then org-wide. add automated revert if degrade_quality_regression > 3% over baseline.
anya: infra question: how do we keep latency SLOs when we add extra decision logic? keep decision path in-service and small: precompute variant cost estimates and cache TTL 60s. decision is just a quick lookup + compare.
infra-bot: canary cluster provisioned: canary-eng-3 (eu-west). scheduled deploy window 02:00-04:00 UTC.
deploy-bot: rolling deploy started to canary-eng-3 for service=router v=2.14.1-canary.
kevin: ops concern: token accounting edge cases with streaming. if we switch mid-stream, cost attribution must be consistent. prefer only switching at request start.
anya: yes, only at request start. streaming switch is out.
lia: mockups: will upload a quick proto in #design by EOD. includes impact modal and quick revert.
sahil: one more: alerting — create "degrade_rate_pct > 20%" for a given org or route, and "savings_vs_baseline < -1%" (i.e., worse cost) to catch incorrect thresholds.
ravin: can we record a small sample of responses from each variant into eval pool automatically for regression detection?
anya: yes, sample 0.1% by default and tie to per-org eval sets. need privacy opt-out option.
kevin: sounds good. next steps: write RFC for policy schema + telemetry fields, then demo in canary. I'll volunteer to draft the RFC.
anya: awesome, thanks. I'll coordinate with lia and sahil for console + metrics. leaving TODOs in the RFC: schema, migration, alert rules, canary list. :white_check_mark:
